name: drg-0011-goal3
goal: Count the neurons and report what fraction of them are CGRP-positive nociceptors.

look.notes: The image is a fluorescence microscopy image of a rat dorsal root ganglion section stained with an antibody against neurofilament, which marks neuronal cell bodies. The three images show different magnifications of the same section. The total number of neurons is estimated to be around 1000 based on the scale and density observed in the whole section (image 1).

not_possible: Counting CGRP-positive nociceptors: The image only shows one fluorescence channel (Neurofilament). There is no CGRP channel or marker visible to split or identify CGRP-positive neurons. Therefore, the fraction of CGRP-positive nociceptors cannot be determined from this image.

steps.why: To identify and outline neuronal cell bodies based on their morphology and neurofilament staining. This will allow counting of neurons.
steps.marker: Neurofilament (single channel, no split possible for CGRP)

steps.why: To count the total number of neurons identified by find_cells. This is the first part of the goal.
steps.marker: Neurofilament (single channel, no split possible for CGRP)

plan.result: The total number of neurons can be counted. However, the fraction of CGRP-positive nociceptors cannot be determined because the CGRP channel is not present in the image.
risks: The neuron size range (5–50 µm) may not capture all neurons, especially smaller or larger ones, leading to undercounting or overcounting.
The single-channel image does not allow for splitting by CGRP, so the fraction of CGRP-positive nociceptors cannot be calculated.
The resolution (pixel size ~1.02 µm) is sufficient for cell body identification but may not resolve fine details of CGRP expression if it were present.
